bib.title: GQA: A New Dataset for Real-World Visual Reasoning and Compositional Question Answering

question: Can a balanced, program-annotated VQA benchmark over real images measure compositional visual reasoning better than accuracy on biased VQA sets?
hypothesis: Existing VQA benchmarks are dominated by answer priors; a scene-graph-generated, answer-balanced dataset with consistency/grounding metrics will expose a large gap to humans.
contributions: the GQA dataset as a resource for studying visual reasoning
a method for generating many semantically varied questions marrying scene graphs with computational linguistic methods
new metrics (consistency, validity, plausibility, distribution, grounding) and a performance analysis of existing models

method.summary: Questions are generated from cleaned Visual Genome scene graphs using 524 patterns and functional programs, balanced by tunable answer-distribution smoothing, then baselines, BottomUp and MAC are trained and evaluated with accuracy plus five new metrics.

datasets.name: GQA
datasets.size: 22,669,678 questions over 113,018 images generated; 1.7M after balancing
datasets.split: 70% train, 10% val, 10% test, 10% challenge; all questions of an image in one split
datasets.source: Visual Genome scene graphs (images from COCO and Flickr) plus 5k hidden crowdsourced scene graphs for test; vocabulary 3097 words, 1878 answers; ontology 1740 objects, 620 attributes, 330 relations, 60 categories
datasets.preprocessing: graph vocab cleaned into 2690-class ontology, edges pruned, positional info added; 524 patterns (250 manual + 274 from VQA1.0), 117 question groups

datasets.name: VQA
datasets.source: VQA 1.0/2.0 used for transfer test and comparison

models.name: Global Prior / Local Prior
models.architecture: most common answer per global / local question group

models.name: CNN (deaf), LSTM (blind), CNN+LSTM
models.architecture: ImageNet-pretrained spatial CNN features; LSTM over GloVe-300 question embeddings; sigmoid classifier

models.name: BottomUp (Anderson et al.)
models.architecture: bottom-up attention over Faster R-CNN object features; own re-implementation

models.name: MAC (Hudson & Manning)
models.architecture: recurrent compositional attention network, 4 cells, official code

other.input: GloVe 300-d; spatial ImageNet features for CNN models, Faster R-CNN object features for BottomUp and MAC
other.shared: all models use the same LSTM, CNN and classifier components

inference.samples: single run per model (seeds not stated)

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: exact match to ground-truth answer, overall and per structural/semantic type

metrics.name: Consistency
metrics.definition: for each correctly answered q, accuracy over its entailed questions E_q, averaged

metrics.name: Validity
metrics.definition: answer is within the question scope (a colour for a colour question)

metrics.name: Plausibility
metrics.definition: answer occurs at least once in relation with the question subject across the dataset

metrics.name: Distribution
metrics.definition: Chi-Square statistic between true and predicted answer distribution

metrics.name: Grounding
metrics.definition: attention probability mass on the annotated region, attention models only

eval.protocol: Test set. Humans: Amazon Mechanical Turk, 4000 random questions, majority of 5 answers.

results.claim: MAC, the best model tested, reaches 54.06% accuracy on GQA test, far below humans at 89.3%.
results.setup: GQA test set, standard split, models trained on GQA balanced training set; human = AMT majority of 5 answers on 4000 random questions
results.note: Abstract rounds to 54.1% (strong VQA models) and 89.3% humans; Table 1 prints 54.06 and 89.3

results.claim: A blind LSTM (question only) gets 41.07% accuracy, so language priors alone go a long way even after balancing.
results.setup: GQA test set, standard split, models trained on GQA balanced training set; LSTM with no image

results.claim: Human consistency is 98.4% while MAC is 81.59% and BottomUp 78.71%; best models contradict themselves on about 1 in 5 entailed questions.
results.setup: GQA test set, standard split, models trained on GQA balanced training set; consistency = accuracy on questions entailed by each correctly answered question, averaged
results.quote: even the best models are inconsistent in about 1 out of 5 questions

results.claim: MAC trained on GQA reaches 52.1% on VQA before fine-tuning and 60.5% after, versus 68.3% for MAC trained and tested on VQA.
results.quote: A MAC model trained on GQA achieves 52.1% on VQA before

results.claim: MAC trained on VQA gets only 39.8% on GQA before fine-tuning and 46.5% after.
Grounding score is 82.24% for MAC and 78.47% for BottomUp; swapping object features for spatial features drops it to 43%.
results.setup: GQA test set, standard split, models trained on GQA balanced training set; attention probability on the annotated region, attention models only
results.note: 43% for spatial features is stated in Sec 4.4 text

results.claim: Models give an invalid or implausible answer at least 5-15% of the time.
results.setup: MAC validity 96.16, plausibility 84.48; LSTM validity 96.39, plausibility 87.30 (Table 1)
Smoothing of answer distribution within question groups, global then local
results.quote: the entropy of the answer distribution is increased by 72%

results.claim: Balanced GQA has 1.7M questions downsampled from 22M generated; splits are 70/10/10/10 train/val/test/challenge, grouped by image.
results.quote: split the dataset into 70% train, 10% valida

results.claim: Only 22.69% of open (query) questions are answered by the LSTM, and the question-group priors score 17-47% overall.
results.setup: GQA test set, standard split, models trained on GQA balanced training set

results.claim: MAC with text questions: 53.8% accuracy, 81.59% consistency; with functional programs as input 59.7% and 85.85%.
results.note: Table 1 prints MAC accuracy 54.06 (test); 53.8 is from a Supp diagnosis run (split not stated)
results.quote: MAC achieves 53.8% accuracy and 81.59% consistency on the textual questions and 59.7% and 85.85%

results.claim: GQA covers 88.8% of VQA questions and 70.6% of VQA answers.
results.note: text: 'covers 88.8% and 70.6% of VQA questions and answers respectively'

results.claim: 52% of GQA questions are compositional versus 3% for VQA 2.0; mean question length 7.9 vs 6.2 words.
results.table: Table 3, row Compositional questions, column GQA

results.claim: Per-model BottomUp re-implementation scores 67% on VQA, matching the original report.
results.setup: Sanity check of own BottomUp re-implementation on VQA
results.quote: achieving 67%, which matches the original scores reported by Anderson et al.

limits: Questions are templated and 'not natural', only factual and answerable from the image; no why/intention, OCR or external-knowledge questions.
Plausibility metric may be imprecise for infrequent objects due to data scarcity (footnote 6).
Grounding only defined for attention models.
No seeds, learning rate or batch size reported; baselines are 2017-2018 models (pre-transformer).
Authors concede training-set size had not saturated.

whether a given answer is in the question scope
whether the answer is reasonable given the question
